Chapter VIII

The Preservation of Savoy College Tradition

ACTIVITIES PRECEDING THE REUNION OF 1938

REVIVAL OF THE REUNION IDEA.—For years Savoy College ex-students talked among themselves about the possibility of having a Reunion. It had been hoped that such plans might materialize during the life times of the founder, Professor R. B. Halsell, and his comrades in the work for many years, Professor Simmons. They had such plans come to a realization, many other beloved faculty members, who have now passed on, could have been present, too.

In the summer of 1937, when with the aid of Federal funds through the Works Progress Administration the Savoy Independent School District was holding a new gymnasium, Mr. Gus W. Thomasson, a WPA foreman in charge of a part of the work, happened to be a grandson of Thomas J., a Savoy College founder and using the occasion of the building's dedication, originated a plan for a reunion of ex-students of the old College.

On August 15, 1937, Mr. Thomasson sent a circular letter to as large a mailing list of former students as he could compile, giving in the letter the history of the old school and suggesting that Mr. W. F. Carter, president of the Savoy School Board and an old Savoy school man himself, was even then ready to begin making plans for a gathering of ex-students to take place at the dedication of the gymnasium planned for the fall. A date in November was set for this. It was also mentioned, incidentally, that the Works Progress Administration, through Mr. Gaber, was even then engaged in compiling a history of Fannin County, of Savoy, and of the old Savoy school. A plea was made that documents, photographs, or relics of interest of the old school to be sent to Mr. Thomasson or Carter.
